Taylor K: Hey team — couple quick onboarding questions: I signed up for medical+vision but I only see medical reflected in Workday. Is vision enrolled separately? Also, I opted into the FSA but want to confirm the annual limit and whether I can change midyear. Finally, do I need to add my spouse as a dependent in two places or just once?

Jasmine (People Ops): Welcome Taylor! :wave: Vision is usually a separate election in the Benefits portal (same provider tab). If you enrolled during the benefits step it should show under "Elections" in Workday within 24h. Spouse needs to be added under Dependents in Workday AND attached on the benefits election screen for the plan to cover them.

Taylor K: Got it. I don't see vision under Elections yet. Enrollment deadline was yesterday so wondering if it's a timing lag. Also, FSA limit?

HR Bot: Benefits enrollment processing: changes can take up to 48 hours to propagate to Workday. FSA limits 2025: Health FSA max $3,050 (annual). Mid-year changes allowed only with a qualifying life event (QLE).

Liam P: If you missed the window and had a qualifying event (marriage/birth), we can reopen. Otherwise next open enrollment. Quick tip: attach spouse's ID and SSN in Workday docs to speed verification.

Taylor K: Thanks. If vision isn't showing after 48h, who do I ping to manually resubmit?

Jasmine (People Ops): Ping me or Benefits Admin here and include your employee ID. We can check the carrier enrollment file and resubmit. If you want immediate access to vision benefits, request a temporary ID via the insurer app (they usually allow e-cards).

Taylor K: One more: I filled out W-4 during onboarding — does Redwood default to state withholding too or do I have to complete a separate state form? I'm in CA.

Benefits Admin: Payroll requires both federal W-4 and state CA DE-4 (or state equivalent) for state withholding. If you didn't submit the state form, Workday will apply default withholding for state which might be higher. You can upload CA DE-4 under Pay > Tax Withholding in Workday.

Taylor K: Perfect, I'll add the state form. Re reimbursements: I have a receipt for home office lighting. Where to submit and what's the turnaround?

Jasmine (People Ops): Submit via Expensify, policy = "newhire-office". People Ops reviews within 3 business days, Finance pays on next AP run (Tue/Thu). Make sure receipt total <= $500 for quick approval (larger items need manager sign-off).

Taylor K: Awesome, thanks everyone :raised_hands:
